title: Monitoring cost per request, per user and per feature

videos.script: The assistant ran for a week. What did it cost? One number answers that, and explains nothing. {{one}} The spans hold tokens, not money. Money is worked out later, from a price list where every price has a start date. Prices change. Tuesday's cost should not. {{prices}} Split by feature, order questions cost the most per request, because a customer writing about their own order writes more. The summaries everybody expected to be dear cost what a help question does. {{feature}} Split by user, the two heaviest users turn out to be the support team. {{user}} Split by day, the cost per request halves in a week. Part of that is a price cut. Most of it is a release that made the assistant answer less. {{day}} Keep tokens and prices apart, and the two causes stay separate. {{apart}} Last, budgets the code checks for itself: one per feature, one per user, and the provider's own limit behind both. {{budget}}
